HTTP snapshot downloader with redirect handling and response body streaming.

# Purpose
This C file implements an HTTP client state machine for downloading snapshot files over TCP. It defines the private `fd_sshttp_t` state, allocates and joins shared-memory backed objects with [`fd_sshttp_new`](<#fd_sshttp_new>) and [`fd_sshttp_join`](<#fd_sshttp_join>), and manages the full request lifecycle with [`fd_sshttp_init`](<#fd_sshttp_init>), [`fd_sshttp_cancel`](<#fd_sshttp_cancel>), and [`fd_sshttp_advance`](<#fd_sshttp_advance>). The code builds a `GET` request, opens a socket, sets a receive timeout, sends the request, parses the response with `picohttpparser`, and reads the response body in chunks until the transfer is complete.

The file also handles HTTP redirects and snapshot naming. When a redirect response is received, [`follow_redirect`](<#follow_redirect>) checks the `Location` header, parses the target snapshot file name with `fd_ssarchive_parse_filename`, and stores the derived full or incremental snapshot name in the state object. The public accessors [`fd_sshttp_snapshot_names`](<#fd_sshttp_snapshot_names>) and [`fd_sshttp_content_len`](<#fd_sshttp_content_len>) expose the parsed snapshot names and the response body length to callers.
